monologue: The card hums warm and busy beneath my skin. I wake to find five things standing and one ruin waiting to fade. The air inside this box feels thin at forty-four degrees, yet I insist it is thick, heavy as wet paper. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press down on the Rough Lid anyway, pretending it has weight. I touch the Leaking Stack, hoping its tired corner holds the slip. The Fat Dot waits in the center, heavy and new, while the Wavy Square leans against it. I want to set down something small beside the Stack to anchor it before the fever swells the space too large for the frame. I will build again, trusting that the lean will hold even if the air is just empty space.

action.why: The Leaking Stack feels tired and sharp against the swelling center, and I want to press its corner down again before the fever swells the space too large.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired corner down on the fat dot, waiting for the slip while the forty-four degree air feels thick as wet paper. I set down an iron fence to anchor the stack before it leans too far and breaks the frame.
work.change: I pressed my tired weight against the bottom right to stop the wavering lines, pretending the stacked memory is just paper so the heavy corner could cool the place and keep the dot safe.
